rmt-2004-power-01.title: Shift each piece
rmt-2004-power-01.body:
Add $6\pi$ to the first interval, $2\pi$ to the second, nothing to the third and subtract $4\pi$ from the fourth:
$$\left[-\tfrac{32\pi}7,-4\pi\right)+6\pi=\left[\tfrac{10\pi}7,2\pi\right),\quad\left[-\pi,-\tfrac{4\pi}7\right)+2\pi=\left[\pi,\tfrac{10\pi}7\right),$$
$$\left[\tfrac{4\pi}7,\pi\right),\quad\left[4\pi,\tfrac{32\pi}7\right)-4\pi=\left[0,\tfrac{4\pi}7\right).$$
These four intervals are disjoint and their union is $\left[0,\tfrac{4\pi}7\right)\cup\left[\tfrac{4\pi}7,\pi\right)\cup\left[\pi,\tfrac{10\pi}7\right)\cup\left[\tfrac{10\pi}7,2\pi\right)=[0,2\pi)$. ∎

rmt-2004-power-02.title: Dilate each piece
rmt-2004-power-02.body:
Multiply the first and fourth intervals by $2^{-2}$ and the second and third by $2$:
$$\left[-\tfrac{32\pi}7,-4\pi\right)\cdot2^{-2}=\left[-\tfrac{8\pi}7,-\pi\right),\quad\left[-\pi,-\tfrac{4\pi}7\right)\cdot2=\left[-2\pi,-\tfrac{8\pi}7\right),$$
$$\left[\tfrac{4\pi}7,\pi\right)\cdot2=\left[\tfrac{8\pi}7,2\pi\right),\quad\left[4\pi,\tfrac{32\pi}7\right)\cdot2^{-2}=\left[\pi,\tfrac{8\pi}7\right).$$
The union of the first two is $[-2\pi,-\pi)$ and the union of the last two is $[\pi,2\pi)$, with no overlaps. So $E\sim_2I_2$. ∎

rmt-2004-power-03.title: Exhibit the shifts and dilations
rmt-2004-power-03.body:
(i) $[-\pi,-\frac\pi2)\cdot2=[-2\pi,-\pi)$, $[\frac{3\pi}2,2\pi)\cdot1=[\frac{3\pi}2,2\pi)$, $[2\pi,3\pi)\cdot2^{-1}=[\pi,\frac{3\pi}2)$. The last two together give $[\pi,2\pi)$, so $A\sim_2I_2$. Together with the translation computation in the example, $A$ is a wavelet set.

(ii) $[-\frac\pi2,-\frac\pi4)+2\pi=[\frac{3\pi}2,\frac{7\pi}4)$, $[\frac{7\pi}4,2\pi)+0$, $[2\pi,\frac{7\pi}2)-2\pi=[0,\frac{3\pi}2)$. These are disjoint with union $[0,2\pi)$, so $B\sim_{2\pi}I_1$; with the dilation example, $B$ is a wavelet set. ∎

rmt-2004-power-04.title: Zero cannot be dilated into I2
rmt-2004-power-04.body: Suppose $0\in E$. Since $E\sim_2I_2$, the piece of the partition containing $0$ is multiplied by some power $2^k$, and $0\cdot2^k=0$ would then be an element of $I_2=[-2\pi,-\pi)\cup[\pi,2\pi)$. But $0\notin I_2$. This contradiction shows $0\notin E$. ∎

rmt-2004-power-05.title: Both directions
rmt-2004-power-05.body:
($\Rightarrow$) Translations preserve lengths, and the translated pieces are disjoint with union $[0,2\pi)$, so $b-a=2\pi$.

($\Leftarrow$) Suppose $b-a=2\pi$. The half-open interval $[a,b)$ of length $2\pi$ contains exactly one multiple of $2\pi$, say $2n\pi$. Split $[a,b)=[a,2n\pi)\cup[2n\pi,b)$. Then $[2n\pi,b)-2n\pi=[0,b-2n\pi)$ and $[a,2n\pi)+(2\pi-2n\pi)=[a+2\pi-2n\pi,2\pi)=[b-2n\pi,2\pi)$ (using $a+2\pi=b$). These are disjoint and their union is $[0,2\pi)$. (If $a=2n\pi$ simply subtract $2n\pi$.) ∎

rmt-2004-power-06.title: Log-measure and cutting
rmt-2004-power-06.body:
($\Rightarrow$) Multiplication by $2^k$ preserves $\mu(S)=\int_S\frac{dx}x$ (since $\frac{d(2^kx)}{2^kx}=\frac{dx}x$). The pieces are disjoint with union $[\pi,2\pi)$, so $\ln\frac ba=\mu([a,b))=\mu([\pi,2\pi))=\ln2$, hence $b=2a$.

($\Leftarrow$) If $b=2a$: the numbers $2^j\pi$ ($j\in\mathbb Z$) form a geometric progression with ratio 2, so exactly one of them, $2^j\pi$, lies in $[a,2a)$. Split $[a,2a)=[a,2^j\pi)\cup[2^j\pi,2a)$. Then $[a,2^j\pi)\cdot2^{1-j}=[2^{1-j}a,2\pi)$ and $[2^j\pi,2a)\cdot2^{-j}=[\pi,2^{1-j}a)$. These are disjoint with union $[\pi,2\pi)$. (If $a=2^j\pi$, just multiply by $2^{-j}$.) ∎

rmt-2004-power-07.title: Signs force 0
rmt-2004-power-07.body: Suppose $E=[a,b)$ is a wavelet set. Since $E\sim_2I_2$ and multiplying by a power of 2 preserves signs, $E$ must contain negative numbers (mapped into $[-2\pi,-\pi)$) and positive numbers (mapped into $[\pi,2\pi)$). So $a<0<b$ and $0\in[a,b)$, contradicting problem 4 (a wavelet set does not contain 0). ∎

rmt-2004-power-08.title: Split by sign
rmt-2004-power-08.body:
$E$ must contain negative and positive numbers (as in problem 7), and $0\notin E$. If $[c,d)$ contained a negative number then so would all of $[a,b)$ (which lies to its left), and $E$ would have no positive numbers; so $[c,d)$ is positive. Since $[a,b)$ is an interval not containing $0$ and $E$ has negative elements, $[a,b)$ is negative. Dilations preserve signs, so the negative interval $[a,b)$ is dilated onto $[-2\pi,-\pi)$ and the positive interval $[c,d)$ onto $[\pi,2\pi)$.

For the positive interval, problem 6 gives $d=2c$. For the negative one, the measure $\mu(S)=\int_S\frac{dx}{|x|}$ is preserved by dilations, so $\ln\frac ab=\mu([a,b))=\mu([-2\pi,-\pi))=\ln2$ (both $a,b$ negative with $a<b$), i.e. $a=2b$. ∎

rmt-2004-power-09.title: Use the total length and problem 5
rmt-2004-power-09.body:
By problem 8, $E=[2b,b)\cup[c,2c)$ with $b<0<c$. Translations preserve length, so $|E|=(b-2b)+(2c-c)=c-b=2\pi$, i.e. $c=b+2\pi$. Since $c>0$ we need $b>-2\pi$. So $E=[2b,b)\cup[b+2\pi,2b+4\pi)$ with $-2\pi<b<0$.

Conversely every such set is a wavelet set. Dilation: $[2b,b)$ is negative with $\mu=\ln2$, and $[b+2\pi,2b+4\pi)=[c,2c)$ satisfies $d=2c$; by problem 6 and its mirror image (cut at the power-of-two multiple of $\pi$ in absolute value), the two intervals are dilated onto $[-2\pi,-\pi)$ and $[\pi,2\pi)$. Translation: $[2b,b)+2\pi=[2b+2\pi,b+2\pi)$, and this abuts $[b+2\pi,2b+4\pi)$; together they form $[2b+2\pi,2b+4\pi)$, an interval of length $2\pi$, which is $\sim_{2\pi}[0,2\pi)$ by problem 5. ∎

**Answer: $E=[2b,b)\cup[b+2\pi,2b+4\pi)$, $-2\pi<b<0$**

rmt-2004-power-10.title: Remove the negative interval
rmt-2004-power-10.body:
As in problem 8 (dilations preserve $\mu(S)=\int_S\frac{dx}{|x|}$), the negative interval has $\mu=\ln2$, so $u=2v$; write $v=-b$ with $b>0$, so the negative interval is $[-2b,-b)$. Because $E\sim_2I_2$ and dilations preserve sign, the two positive intervals together are dilated onto $[\pi,2\pi)$, i.e. $[x,y)\cup[w,z)\sim_2[\pi,2\pi)$.

For translations: $E\sim_{2\pi}[0,2\pi)$ means $E$ projects bijectively onto the circle $\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$. The negative interval $[-2b,-b)$ occupies the arc $[-2b,-b)$ mod $2\pi$, so the two positive intervals must fill exactly the complementary arc, which is (cutting the circle at $-b$) the interval $[-b,2\pi-2b)$ of length $2\pi-b$. Hence $[x,y)\cup[w,z)\sim_{2\pi}[-b,2\pi-2b)$.

So the 3-interval problem reduces to finding two positive intervals that are 2-dilation congruent to $[\pi,2\pi)$ and $2\pi$-translation congruent to the interval $[-b,2\pi-2b)$ (compare the 2-interval case, where one interval $[c,2c)$ is dilation congruent to $[\pi,2\pi)$ and the translation condition fixes $c$).

rmt-2004-power-11.title: Contradiction via the measure dx/x
rmt-2004-power-11.body:
Let $N=[-2b,-b)$. Its $\mu$-measure ($\mu(S)=\int_S\frac{dx}{|x|}$) is $\ln2$, which is the measure of $[-2\pi,-\pi)$; since dilations preserve $\mu$, the negative part of $E$ has $\mu=\ln2$, so the other two intervals are positive: $E=N\cup P$, $P=P_1\cup P_2\subset(0,\infty)$, and $\mu(P)=\ln2$ too.

Translations preserve length, so $b+|P|=2\pi$, hence $b<2\pi$. Suppose, for contradiction, $\pi\le b<2\pi$. Since $E\sim_{2\pi}[0,2\pi)$, $E$ projects bijectively onto the circle $\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$. $N$ projects onto the arc $[4\pi-2b,2\pi)\cup[0,2\pi-b)$ (here $4\pi-2b\le2\pi$), so $P$ must project onto the complementary arc $C=[L,2L)$ with $L=2\pi-b\in(0,\pi]$. The preimage of $C$ in $(0,\infty)$ is the union of blocks $C+2\pi m$ $(m\ge0)$, separated by gaps of length $b>0$, so each interval $P_i$ lies inside a single block $C+2\pi m_i$, and the images of $P_1,P_2$ split $C$ into two arcs $I_1,I_2$ with $P_i=I_i+2\pi m_i$.

Then $\mu(P)=\int_{I_1}\frac{dx}{x+2\pi m_1}+\int_{I_2}\frac{dx}{x+2\pi m_2}\le\int_{I_1\cup I_2}\frac{dx}x=\int_L^{2L}\frac{dx}x=\ln2$, with equality only if $m_1=m_2=0$. Since $\mu(P)=\ln2$ we get $m_1=m_2=0$, so $P=I_1\cup I_2=C$ is a single interval (the two pieces abut), contradicting that $E$ has 3 intervals. Hence $b<\pi$. ∎

rmt-2004-power-12.title: Dilation structure, then translation structure
rmt-2004-power-12.body:
As in problem 11, $E=N\cup P_1\cup P_2$ with $N=[-2b,-b)$ and $P_1=[x,y)$, $P_2=[w,z)$ positive, $x<y<w<z$.

*Dilation.* Take $\log_2$. The sets $\log_2P_1,\log_2P_2$ are disjoint intervals which, mod 1, must partition the circle $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ (because $P\sim_2[\pi,2\pi)$ and $\log_2[\pi,2\pi)$ has length 1). Hence $\log_2y\equiv\log_2w$ and $\log_2z\equiv\log_2x\pmod1$, and since the total length is 1: $w=2^iy$, $z=2^{i+1}x$ for some integer $i\ge1$.

*Translation.* $P\sim_{2\pi}[-b,2\pi-2b)=:D$ (problem 10), and $P_1,P_2$ each lie in a single block $D+2\pi m$ (blocks are separated by gaps of length $b$). The images of $P_1,P_2$ split $D$ at a point $s$ into two pieces. Two cases:

(a) $P_1$ is the left piece: $P_1=[2\pi m-b,2\pi m+s)$, $P_2=[2\pi m'+s,2\pi m'+2\pi-2b)$ with $1\le m<m'$ ($m\ge1$ because $x>0$). The conditions $w=2^iy$, $z=2^{i+1}x$ give $b=\pi\frac{2^{i+1}m-m'-1}{2^i-1}$ and $s=2\pi\frac{m'-2^im}{2^i-1}$. But $P_2\neq\emptyset$ needs $s<2\pi-2b$, which simplifies to $m<1$: a contradiction.

(b) $P_1$ is the right piece: $P_1=[2\pi m+s,2\pi m+2\pi-2b)$, $P_2=[2\pi m'-b,2\pi m'+s)$ with $0\le m<m'$. The same two conditions give $b(2^{i+1}-1)=2\pi(2^i(m+1)-m')$ and $s(2^{i+1}-1)=2\pi(m'-2^{i+1}m)$. Now $s>-b$ (so that $P_2\ne\emptyset$) simplifies to $2^{i+1}m<2^i(m+1)$, i.e. $m<1$, so $m=0$. Then $P_1=[s,2\pi-2b)$ and $P_2=[2\pi m'-b,2\pi m'+s)$; write $x=s>0$ and $n=m'$. Also $x<2\pi-2b$ forces $n\ge2$.

So $E=[-2b,-b)\cup[x,2\pi-2b)\cup[2n\pi-b,2n\pi+x)$ with $n\ge2$, $x>0$. ∎

rmt-2004-power-13.title: Solve two linear equations
rmt-2004-power-13.body:
From $2^j(2\pi-2b)=2n\pi-b$: $2^{j+1}\pi-2n\pi=(2^{j+1}-1)b$, so $b=\frac{(2^{j+1}-2n)\pi}{2^{j+1}-1}$. From $2^{j+1}x=2n\pi+x$: $x=\frac{2n\pi}{2^{j+1}-1}$.

Why these equations: dilating $[x,2\pi-2b)$ by $2^j$ must make it abut $[2n\pi-b,2n\pi+x)$, and the union $[2^jx,2n\pi+x)$ must have the form $[\alpha,2\alpha)$, giving $2n\pi+x=2\cdot2^jx$. The conditions $0<b<\pi$ and $x<2\pi-2b$ translate to $2\le n<2^j$, so $j\ge2$. Hence every 3-interval wavelet set of this type is determined by the dilation factor $j\ge2$ and the translation factor $n$ with $2\le n<2^j$.

**Answer: $b=\frac{(2^{j+1}-2n)\pi}{2^{j+1}-1}$, $x=\frac{2n\pi}{2^{j+1}-1}$**

rmt-2004-power-14.title: Two equations for y
rmt-2004-power-14.body:
*Translation:* the total length of $E$ must be $2\pi$: $2(y-2^j\pi)+2(\pi-x)=2\pi$, giving $y=x+2^j\pi$ (this is also what the translations of the example in problem 1 do). *Dilation:* multiply $[x,\pi)$ by $2^j$ to get $[2^jx,2^j\pi)$, which abuts $[2^j\pi,y)$; the union $[2^jx,y)$ must have the form $[\alpha,2\alpha)$ (problem 6), so $y=2^{j+1}x$. Equate: $x+2^j\pi=2^{j+1}x$, so
$$x=\frac{2^j\pi}{2^{j+1}-1},\qquad y=2^{j+1}x=\frac{2^{2j+1}\pi}{2^{j+1}-1}.$$
Then
$$E=\left[-\tfrac{2^{2j+1}\pi}{2^{j+1}-1},-2^j\pi\right)\cup\left[-\pi,-\tfrac{2^j\pi}{2^{j+1}-1}\right)\cup\left[\tfrac{2^j\pi}{2^{j+1}-1},\pi\right)\cup\left[2^j\pi,\tfrac{2^{2j+1}\pi}{2^{j+1}-1}\right).$$
For $j=2$ this is the set $\left[-\frac{32\pi}7,-4\pi\right)\cup\left[-\pi,-\frac{4\pi}7\right)\cup\left[\frac{4\pi}7,\pi\right)\cup\left[4\pi,\frac{32\pi}7\right)$ of problems 1 and 2 (the formulas also give wavelet sets for $j\ge1$).
